Two memo illustrations (p24 top-right, p25 foot) are measured rasters and are excluded as page furniture. doc_order is the builder's reading order over regions, so on p10 it puts Figure 3 (right panel, y92) before Figure 2 (left panel, y96.5). three_d is recorded 'isometric' on the four surfaces and on Figure 16 rather than 'surface-mesh' because the drawn object is a discrete point lattice over a filled contour floor, not a shaded continuous mesh; P-C-2022-2218931 (lane rows 8-9) is the contrast case where the same tool draws true meshes.
rules: Caption side is decided by exhibit type, not by taste: all sixteen figure captions print BELOW their artwork and all grid captions print ABOVE their grid, without exception across 19 rows [caption.position].

Every caption on this paper is a bare noun phrase - no finite verb, no unit, no named variable except on Figure 16, no conclusion - so voice is 'none' on all nineteen, and the only three captions that state anything beyond the object state which parameter was held fixed [caption.voice] [caption.variables] [caption.units] [caption.concludes] [caption.conditions].

Four plates carry the words 'Schematic diagram' or 'flow chart' in the caption but only two (Figures 1 and 9) are schematics; Figures 10, 12 and 15 are line and bar charts. The caption's noun is not evidence of the family - read the drawing [geometry.family] [caption.verbatim].

The paper reuses one plate template for all four parameter surfaces: a perspective point grid over a filled jet contour floor with a right-hand colour scale, differing only in which parameter is held fixed and in the colour range (0-113500, 0-92500, 894-1510, 986-1680) [geometry.three_d] [geometry.colorbar] [geometry.family].
Three-dimensional plates appear five times - the four parameter surfaces and Figure 16 - and no caption ever says three-dimensional; the word 'surface' never appears in the paper [geometry.three_d].

Colour bars exist only on the four surfaces. Everywhere else colour is identity: in-panel keys at upper-left on seven rows, and in Figure 9 colour is used only for two lightning marks [geometry.colorbar] [geometry.legend].

Insets are this paper's substitute for panels: five plates (Figures 4, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12) carry a dashed callout box and a magnified re-plot of one short window, and only Figures 8, 11 and 15 put two real panels side by side [geometry.panel_count] [geometry.panel_layout].
No plate shares an axis with its neighbour: paired panels always differ in level (bitcoin 0-60000 against gold 0-6000 in Figure 11) so the reader compares shape, not magnitude [geometry.shared_axes].

Printed numbers are reserved for readings the text then quotes: every endpoint asset value, the earnings difference, the per-trade amounts in Bitcoins and troy ounces, and the annualised returns in Figure 14. Only the surfaces carry printed numbers that the text never repeats [geometry.printed_numbers] [geometry.data_labels].

Pointing is locative and number-bearing: eleven rows use 'as shown in Figure N', five use 'Figure N shows/the following figure', and only Figures 1 and 7 are never cited by number - Figure 1 has no prose mention at all [mention.lead_pattern] [mention.style] [mention.count].

Pairs share one pointing sentence: Figures 2+3 and Figures 5+6 are each announced by a single clause ('as shown in Figure 2 and Figure 3', 'shown in Figure 5 and Figure 6'), so a per-exhibit mention count doubles a sentence that was written once [mention.lead_sentence] [mention.count].

Reading sentences are optional but formulaic when present: 'The following features can be seen in Figure N.', 'From the above figure, we can see that', 'The following conclusions can be drawn from Figure N.' - and on Figures 5 and 6 the reading sentence prints a page AFTER the plate, not beside it [mention.trail_sentence] [mention.read_sentences].
Only Figure 4 is announced a page early (pointer at the foot of p10, plate at the head of p11); every other pointer sits on the exhibit's page [mention.first_page] [mention.lead_pages].
All grids are booktabs - rules above and below the header and below the body, no vertical rules - and never boxed [table.rule_style].

Zebra striping is used where the grid is long enough to need row tracking (Table 1's seven-row notation list, Table 2's seven-row factor table) and dropped where it is not (Table 4's two rows, Table 3's two formula rows) [table.zebra].

Column count follows the comparison the paper makes, not the page: Table 2 doubles every measurement into a bitcoin and a gold column (7 columns for 3 factors) while Table 4 keeps one measurement per plan (4 columns for 2 plans) [table.cols] [table.rows].

Units are handled three different ways in four grids and never consistently: a separate Unit column (Table 1), units implied in the header words (Table 2), a unit inside one header cell (Table 4) and none at all (Table 3) [table.units_in_header] [table.decimal_aligned]

No grid in the paper is continued, merged, diagonal-headed or annotated with a note row; Table 1 is the one apparent exception and it only crosses a page break, with no repeated header on its second page [table.continued] [table.merged_cells] [table.diagonal_header] [table.note_sentence]
